extracted.intended_audience: researchers and research administrators searching for NWO funding opportunities (Netherlands)
extracted.subtask_description: Finding and filtering NWO (Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research) funding calls and reading per-call metadata and aims to identify suitable grant opportunities. The page provides status definitions, filter dimensions (type, programme, theme, discipline, target groups) and brief call summaries (status, budget, opening/submission dates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Call status definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief explanation per status: In preparation; Upcoming; Open for applications / letter of intent / pre-proposals; In progress; Continuous; Closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In preparation: pre-announcements of calls NWO expects to publish. Upcoming: calls that have been notified to the Government Gazette (in Dutch: Staatscourant) and will open after publication on the NWO website. Open for applications / letter of intent / pre-proposals: NWO may ask for a letter of intent and/or a pre-proposal to be submitted prior to the full application. In progress: the application procedure has started. Submitting applications is no longer possible. Continuous: a funding request can often be submitted at several points in the year. Closed: the application process is now closed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filterable dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Search and filter calls by key dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is possible to filter by disciplines, status (upcoming, open or closed), form of financing or on for whom the calls are specifically designed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of funding (funding line objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: NWO provides a limited palette of funding lines, each with its own distinctive objective; type-of-funding is a primary classification dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown: Collaboration with Partners; Applied Science; Curiosity Driven Research; Talent Development; Infrastructure; Programme. Proposers should select the funding line whose distinctive objective best matches their project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme (programme-level classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls are grouped under programmes and programme clusters which represent thematic or strategic funding tracks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed include Knowledge and Innovation Covenant; Partnerships (KIC 2020-2023); KIA Societal Earning Capacity (KIC); Dutch Research Agenda (NWA); Thematic Programming; NWO Talent Programme; National Growth Fund; European Partnerships; International programmes. Each programme entry often carries its own aims, eligibility and timelines (see individual programme pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Target groups / 'About specific subjects'
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls can be targeted to specific applicant groups or collaboration types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter examples: Starting Researchers; Collaboration with Industry; Collaboration with social partners; Diversity; International Collaboration; Applied Sciences Research; Knowledge Utilisation; Interdisciplinary Collaboration; Researchers from Abroad; Teachers. Use these facets to identify calls aimed at particular career stages, partnership models, or institutional roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme (subject-matter focus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls are categorised by topical themes to match subject-matter relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example themes: Artificial Intelligence; Biodiversity; Climate; Diversity and Inclusion; Education; Energy; Food; Health; Key Technologies; Knowledge Utilisation; Resilient Society; Safety; Sustainable Cities; Sustainability; Water. Choose themes to find calls aligned with the proposal's topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline (academic domain classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls are also filterable by academic discipline to reflect domain-specific suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example disciplines: Environmental science; Science and technology; Technology; Economics; Computer science; Geography/planning; Life sciences; Sociology; Chemistry; Biology; Earth sciences; Public administration & political science; Business administration; Law; Communication science; Psychology; Physics; Mathematics; and many more. Use discipline filters to locate calls relevant to the research field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-call metadata fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual call listings provide standardized metadata about each call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metadata shown in listings includes: Status (e.g., Continuous, In preparation), Opening date / upcoming opening date, Upcoming submission date, Budget (where stated), and a short description of the call's aim and eligible applicant types. These fields help quickly assess applicability and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal submission stages and required pre-submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some calls require staged application processes (letters of intent, pre-proposals) before full proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site notes that for calls labelled 'Open for applications / letter of intent / pre-proposals', NWO may ask for a letter of intent and/or a pre-proposal to be submitted prior to the full application. Applicants must check the call-specific instructions for required stages and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call aim / 'The aim of...' statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Many calls include an explicit 'aim' statement describing the kind of research and outcomes the call is intended to support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: 'The Open Technology Programme provides funding for free and unrestricted applied and technical-scientific research without disciplinary boundaries. The programme offers companies and other organizations an accessible way to participate in…' and 'The aim of KIEM Arbeidsbesparende AI is to conduct (explorative) applied research through new practice-oriented research activities focused on the application of testable and existing AI applications (use cases) in…'. These aim statements function as eligibility/fit criteria applicants should match to maximize chance of suitability.
